sentences.text: The Plaintiff's case is that it is a company which is an association of various members, including six TUV companies, which use the umbrella trademark 'TUV'.
The Plaintiff is an association of entities engaged in the manufacture and sale of steam boilers, established in 1938 as an organisation in Germany.
It was meant for creation of uniform technical standards and to improve the safety of boiler systems and other allied industrial systems.
17. Over the years, the Plaintiff-Association has expanded its services to products of all kinds including technical systems, services, operational processes, vehicles and other services.
The companies under the umbrella of 'TUV' claim to support technological innovations and offer services of testing, inspection and certification under the umbrella brand 'TUV'.

The member-companies who form part of the Plaintiff-Association, carry out testing, inspection and certification for various products and technical systems across industries, including food safety and management, medical devices and other quality management systems.
18. The Plaintiff's claim is that 'TUV' is one of the most sought-after and trusted brands for food safety management system standards.
TUV Companies are stated to have their presence in more than 100 countries, including India.
They hold accreditations worldwide and can carry out tests This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 16:41:39 under the licenses to test recognition issued by various government agencies.
The entities themselves are several in number, but the use of the 'TUV' brand by them, brings them under one umbrella.
Thus, TUV certification can be issued by all member entities of the Plaintiff-Association.

In India, it is claimed that TUV has had its presence since 1989, and various events and exhibitions in which it has participated have been set out in the plaint at paras 12-13.
19.
The mark 'TUV' has also been registered since 2003 with user claims dating back to 1st September, 1999 in Classes 41 and 42.

According to the Plaintiff, its predecessors adopted the mark in 1938 and thus, the organisation has a legacy of more than eight decades under the said trademark with total experience of more than 160 years in the field of testing, inspection and certification.

sentences.text: 'TUV' since 1938, the said mark has gained global reputation.
In any event, in India, the mark is registered and the Plaintiff enjoys statutory and common law rights due to extensive use.
The Plaintiff also gave an opportunity to the Defendant, and notified it of the rights it has enjoyed.

However, the explanation for the use of the mark 'TUVINDOCERT' given by the Defendant is set out below:-
"5.

That, the word, "TUVINDOCERT" is novel and unique, which has been derived by joining the following words, i.e.,"Tu", which is a pronoun that means "you" in several Romance languages, including Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian, "Vindo", which is the present participle of the Portuguese verb "vir," which means "to come", which is to be interpreted as "coming" or "being in the process of coming" and "Cert", which is an abbreviation for the word "certified," which means officially recognized as having a particular status or qualification.

Based on these component parts,
"TUVINDOCERT" is to be interpreted as a word that means "you who are coming and are certified".
27.
A perusal of the above explanation shows that the Defendant seeks to conduct a reverse analysis to proffer an explanation for adopting the mark 'TUVINDOCERT'.
The manner in which the brand itself is being broken up / dissected and the adoption is sought to be justified, clearly indicates that the same is not a valid and genuine explanation.
It is nothing but an after- thought justification by someone who has adopted the mark, prima facie, in This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 16:41:39 a dishonest manner.

The Defendant's website also shows that they are claiming to offer certification to third parties, which could also result in enormous confusion, inasmuch as unknown entities may obtain certification presuming the same to be originating from the Plaintiff.

28. Finally, the Defendant's adoption of the mark 'TUVINDOCERT' is also quite recent, as is clear from the date of the change of name i.e. 27th June, 2022, and the fact that the trademark application filed by the Defendant on 7th August, 2022 is based on a proposed-to-be-used basis.

29. Owing to the long, statutory and common rights enjoyed by the Plaintiff in the mark 'TUV' and the fact that enormous damage would be caused by issuing certification by the Defendant under the mark, the Defendant shall stand restrained from using the mark and name 'TUVINDOCERT' or the impugned logos extracted above for its services.
30. The website operated under the domain name www.tuvindocert.com shall also be taken down.
The Domain Name Registrar shall be notified of this order who shall lock and suspend the said domain name.
31. Insofar as the Defendant's corporate name is concerned, the relief qua the same shall be considered after pleadings are completed in the application for interim injunction.
